title: Financial Innovation 2025 review — realized volatility forecasting 綜述

scope.question: 2025 時點的 realized volatility forecasting 文獻主線，對 VolPred 下一步最值得測什麼？
scope.search_window: core review papers through 2025 plus recent benchmark empirical papers
inclusion_rule: must explicitly discuss realized volatility forecasting or directly benchmark RV forecasting models
prefer open-access or publisher-hosted abstracts/full text
exclusion_rule: pure latent-volatility papers with no RV forecasting angle
non-verifiable citation aggregators as evidence source

sources.title: Advances in forecasting realized volatility: a review of methodologies
key_points: surveys publicly available studies from 2000 to H1 2024
covers 32 linear, ML, and DL model families
explicitly excludes latent-volatility models such as standard GARCH when RV is not the modeled target
highlights model-class fragmentation and future-research gaps

sources.title: Prediction of realized volatility and implied volatility indices using AI and machine learning: A review
key_points: systematic review of AI/ML forecasting papers for realized and implied volatility
asks whether AI materially beats traditional econometric benchmarks
flags limited explainable-AI usage and uneven benchmarking discipline

sources.title: Forecasting realized volatility: A review
sources.venue: Journal of the Korean Statistical Society
key_points: canonical older review of HAR-class, MIDAS, realized GARCH, HEAVY, jumps, breaks, and forecast evaluation
useful baseline for what 2025 reviews add versus what was already known

sources.title: Forecasting realized volatility: Does anything beat linear models?
key_points: additional predictors help daily and weekly OOS forecasts
no general statistical evidence that nonlinear ML dominates linear models
monthly economic-value results favor simpler models

sources.title: Combining realized volatility estimators based on economic performance
key_points: economic-performance-weighted forecast combinations outperform statistical combinations
advantage is strongest in crisis and high-volatility periods
pushes the literature beyond pure MSE / QLIKE ranking toward application-aware evaluation

sources.title: Dynamics in Realized Volatility Forecasting: Evaluating GARCH Models and Deep Learning Algorithms Across Parameter Variations
key_points: forecast ranking changes with realized-measure choice and training-size setup
5-minute RV worked best for GARCH-type models in that study
MedRV worked best for deep-learning models in that study

project_lineage.relevance: HAR-type decomposition on TAIFEX produced a null result, reminding us not to overclaim RV feature tweaks without formal significance.
Recent HAR-Quantile work exposed fairness and bootstrap pitfalls; any K1428 follow-up must lock target/loss fairness before claiming improvements.
research_program already marks HAR-RV / Realized GARCH / Realized GJR as blocked mainly by 5-minute data depth; K1428 should sharpen which one to test first once data accumulates.

findings.claim: 2025 literature does not justify a blanket 'DL beats HAR / linear RV models' conclusion.
findings.detail: Recent reviews and benchmark studies converge on a narrower claim: nonlinear or deep models can win in some datasets or horizons, but general statistical dominance over strong linear RV baselines is not established.

findings.claim: Benchmark discipline remains the central bottleneck, not model novelty.
findings.detail: The persistent comparison problems are target mismatch, inconsistent loss functions, weak statistical testing, and selective benchmark choice. This matches VolPred's recent K1421/K1422 lessons.

findings.claim: Economic-value evaluation is a live edge where the literature is thinner and more actionable than another generic accuracy horse race.
findings.detail: Statistical gains do not automatically translate to portfolio or risk-management value. Combination methods tuned to economic objectives look more promising than chasing small average-loss improvements.

findings.claim: The realized-measure choice is model-interacting, not a harmless preprocessing detail.
findings.detail: Recent evidence suggests model rankings can shift when using 5-minute RV versus robust alternatives like MedRV. Follow-up experiments should treat measurement choice as a first-order design dimension.

findings.claim: For VolPred's current data and tooling constraints, the first post-review experiment should favor disciplined linear/high-frequency baselines over transformer-first exploration.
findings.detail: Because local 5-minute history is still shallow, the best near-term research path is a fair HAR-RV / Realized-GARCH / HEAVY baseline study, not a data-hungry deep architecture race.

methodology_risks.why_it_matters: HAR-RV / Realized GARCH forecast RV-type targets; comparing them to close-to-close GARCH on mismatched targets creates mechanical wins.
methodology_risks.mitigation: force same target family or use proxy-robust comparison rules documented in experiment-preamble.md

methodology_risks.why_it_matters: MSE, RMSE, QLIKE, VaR, and economic utility often rank models differently.
methodology_risks.mitigation: pre-register primary loss and secondary risk/economic criteria

methodology_risks.why_it_matters: many benchmark papers report average-loss gains without equally strong multiple-testing control.
methodology_risks.mitigation: DM/Harvey or bootstrap procedures must be part of follow-up design

methodology_risks.why_it_matters: deep architectures can look competitive only in longer/high-frequency panels; shallow local data will bias against a fair read.
methodology_risks.mitigation: do not start with transformer-heavy tests until 5-minute history is adequate

recommended_followups.why: best match to current backlog and strongest literature-supported baseline question
recommended_followups.design: same asset set, same 5-minute realized-measure target family, QLIKE + DM/Harvey + VaR/ES where feasible

recommended_followups.why: S6 implies measurement choice may flip rankings
recommended_followups.design: hold model class fixed, vary realized-measure construction only

recommended_followups.why: S5 suggests higher payoff than another pure-accuracy bake-off
recommended_followups.design: compare statistical combinations versus utility / risk-management weighted combinations

recommended_followups.why: only after baseline fairness and data sufficiency are secured
recommended_followups.design: HAR-RV or Realized-GARCH as locked baseline, then test one restrained ML extension rather than a model zoo

verdict.label: ACTIONABLE_REVIEW
verdict.summary: K1428 does not find a clean literature mandate to jump straight into deep models. The stronger 2025 conclusion is to harden benchmark fairness, target alignment, and economic-value evaluation, then test high-frequency linear RV baselines first.
